items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I think the vast American audience is listening to Rod whatever his name is [Stewart] and Prince and Mick Jagger and Madonna.

ctx.x: A lot of guys did that, didn’t they?

That’s what it was in those days. Largely today too. [laughter] When Sammy Kaye died, I got an awful lot of calls, “What do . . . I said, “I have nothing to say. He wasn’t in the same business I’m in.” They said, “Well, he had a band.” I said, “So did Sousa. It’s nothing to do with what I do, or did. So if you want a comment, well, there he is. I can’t talk about his music. I don’t consider it music.” But it’s dance music. It’s a functional form that people can dance and jump up and down to. Daddy, I want a…
